name: VoxPoser
one_liner: Synthesizes 3D voxel affordance and obstacle value maps from language instructions, then solves for collision-free robot trajectories via MPC.

loop.proposes: An LLM writes Python expressions that compose open-vocabulary vision masks into 3D voxel grids of target attractors, obstacles, and rotation/gripper maps.
loop.judged_by: A deterministic sampling-based Model Predictive Control (MPC) trajectory optimizer and inverse-kinematics solver compute minimum-cost paths over the 3D field.
loop.steers: MPC replans at each step from the current observation; the value map comes from cached model-written code.

headline_result: Zero-shot execution of 25 everyday manipulation tasks across real-world and simulated robot arms with 88% success, plus online adaptation to moving obstacles.
caveat: Voxel grid resolution (e.g. 100^3) limits fine sub-millimeter insertion tasks.
beyond_harness_note: The LLM compiles instructions into a 3D potential field while a deterministic MPC trajectory optimizer solves the continuous control problem.
algorithmic_authority: Model Predictive Control (MPC) trajectory planner and IK solver

sources.title: VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models (CoRL 2023 / arXiv:2307.05973)

verification.notes: Checked against Huang et al., CoRL 2023.
